commands.name: add
commands.task: onboard a repository, on GitHub or on this machine
usage: lingtai add [<owner>/<repo>] [flags]
A GitHub repository the App is installed on, or — with no
argument, or --local <dir> — a git checkout on this machine.
--github <owner>/<repo>   same as the positional
--local <dir>             a directory on this machine instead
--project <github|local>  answers the question above, when neither
a slug nor --local is given
--github-app <create|skip>
create or skip the App, asked only when none is configured
--github-auth <gh|app>
how this machine reaches GitHub, asked when nothing is set or none:
the signed-in gh login, or the App. gh is checked, not trusted
--main <branch>
the branch the recipe governs and merges into (branch.main).
A recipe's own branch.main contradicting it is refused.
default: the repository's own default branch
(--base is the old name for this flag, and is refused)
--mode <team|solo>
does anyone else work on this repository? team is the default:
Lingtai works on a personal branch and you send main a PR
--login <login>
team mode on a machine that does not know your GitHub login:
the issues assigned to it are the ones taken
--personal <branch>
team mode: the branch Lingtai works on, yours alone. default:
<login>/<machine>, or lingtai-base for a local project
--tickets <github|db>
where tickets come from, instead of being asked. local takes
db only (#396)
--kinds <a,b,c>
which labels are work, first taken first.
default: bug, feature, tech-debt, documentation
--agent <claude-code|codex>  which agent writes the change
--model <name>, or --model ''
the writer's model; '' for the runtime's own default
--reviewer <agent|none>      a cold reviewer, and which, or none
--reviewer-model <name>, or --reviewer-model ''
the reviewer's model; '' for the runtime's own default
--install <cmd>              what prepares a worktree, e.g. npm ci
--build <cmd|none>           a check that must pass before review;
repeat it for more than one
--check-build yes|no         try install and build once first;
--defaults skips it unless yes
--land <branch|hold>
where an attempt lands, or hold every one for a person at proposed
--refusal-fixes <n>          fixes after a refusal an attempt may buy
--conflict-resolutions <n>   merge conflict resolutions an attempt may buy
--wall <duration>            wall time per agent run, e.g. 1h
--budget <usd>               a dollar ceiling per agent run
--defaults, --yes
use the default of every question whose answer was detected or is
easy to change later. With no terminal, this
or an answer to every question is required. Before anything is
registered the checks and the landing are printed, and a run
that took the defaults for an empty build or an unattended
landing stops there unless --defaults named it

commands.name: run
commands.task: take the queue, in the recipe’s priority order
usage: lingtai run <project> [flags]
--issue <n>   one nominated issue instead of the queue
--max <n>     stop after n items
continues what you approved first, then takes the queue
--once        the same as --max 1
--no-merge    stop after the steps and ask before merging

commands.name: status
commands.task: what is runnable, and what is holding the rest
usage: lingtai status [<project>] [--all] [--json] [--no-color]
Takes nothing and claims nothing.
--all   include items that have left the queue, and why
--json  one document instead of the sections

commands.name: now
commands.task: ask for one ticket ahead of the queue
usage: lingtai now <project> --issue <n> [--json] [--no-color]

commands.name: pr
commands.task: what a team project’s draft holds, and where its open PR is
usage: lingtai pr [<project>] [--json] [--no-color]
The draft, which is the next PR, not yet submitted: the tickets landed
since the last PR was frozen. And the open PR: its number, its state
and the steps it has been through.
A solo project has no PR page: it lands on branch.main itself.
lingtai pr submit [<project>] [--json] [--no-color]
Freezes branch.personal at one commit and starts the PR. Refused
while another PR is open, saying which, and in a solo project. Refused
with nothing landed, and records nothing. Tickets the frozen commit
does not hold stay in the draft for the next PR. A submit Lingtai
cannot carry out returns the PR to the draft, keeping its number, and
says why.
It is served by a running conductor: lingtai start, or lingtai run.
lingtai pr retry [<project>] [--pr <n>] [--json] [--no-color]
Check a waiting PR again: after resolving a conflict by hand on the
PR branch, or after re-running a workflow on GitHub. The conductor
takes the branch as you pushed it if it still holds the frozen commit.
lingtai pr rounds [<project>] [--pr <n>] [--json] [--no-color]
Give the conflict agent 3 more rounds for the main commit the PR
waits on. Refused for any wait that is not a conflict.
lingtai pr back [<project>] [--json] [--no-color]
Take the PR back to Draft: closes the draft pull request on GitHub.
Its tickets join the draft. Refused while a step runs.
lingtai pr summary [<project>] [--file <path>] [--json] [--no-color]
Prints the open PR’s summary. --file replaces it with the file’s text
and waits for the description to be pushed to GitHub. Only the summary
is yours: the ticket lines and Closes lines are regenerated. Refused
for a PR that is merged or closed.

commands.name: attach
commands.task: follow a run’s log, from the beginning
usage: lingtai attach <runId>
What a run is doing, as it does it, however late you attach.
Reads a file and asks nothing of the daemon or the database, so
it answers on a stopped system. A landed run has no log: 0034
keeps exactly the ones still owed an explanation.

commands.name: backlog
commands.task: the minor findings passing steps raised
usage: lingtai backlog [<project>] [--all] [--json] [--no-color]
The open ones. --all adds the decided ones, and what was decided.
lingtai backlog accept <project> <key> --kind <kind> [--unheld]
Open one as an issue through the ticket store. One key: there is
no accept-all. Without --kind, opens the issue of an entry
already accepted — safe to repeat, never a second.
--unheld   without lingtai:hold, so the next turn may take it
lingtai backlog decline <project> <key> --reason <why>
Recorded, so the next attempt does not ask again.

commands.name: report
commands.task: what the pipeline did over a window of days
usage:
lingtai report [--window today|7d] [--kind ] [--project

]
[--json] [--no-color]

lingtai report --from --to [--kind ] [--project

]
Tickets landed, closed and open, the refusal fixes and cost of the
landed ones, spend by kind, and the tickets that went round most.
--window <w>    today, or 7d: the last seven days (the default)
--from <date>   first day of a range, as YYYY-MM-DD, local time
--to <date>     last day of it, included; with --from, never with
--window
--kind <k>      one kind; unclassified tickets are left out

--project

one project; every project by default
--json          one document instead of the sections
Only reads: it changes nothing, and a projection that is behind
is said on stderr while the figures are still printed.

commands.name: ticket
commands.task: a project’s own tickets, where the recipe keeps them
usage:
lingtai ticket list [--all] [--project

] [--json] [--no-color]
Only for a project whose recipe keeps tickets in Lingtai's
database (source.tickets: db); GitHub-backed ones are read with
gh issue list. Open ones by default; --all adds closed ones.

lingtai ticket close [--project

]
Closes that row — not lingtai close, which ends a work item on
the log. The daemon drops it on its next sweep, not at once.

lingtai ticket new [--project

]
Opens $VISUAL or $EDITOR on a form: a title, a labels: line, a
blocked by: line (ticket numbers, e.g. 3, 5), then the body.
Quitting with the form unchanged does nothing. No kind
label and the ticket is created with a warning the queue will
not take it.
lingtai ticket new --title <t> [--label <a,b>] [--blocked-by <n,n>]
No editor: creates the ticket from the flags. --body - reads the
body from stdin. --label, --blocked-by and --body need --title.
--blocked-by names tickets this one waits for; each must exist.

lingtai ticket edit [--project

]
The same form, started from the ticket; writes what changed,
including its blocked by: line.

--project

is required with more than one project registered.
examples: lingtai ticket new --title "Fix the footer link" --label bug

commands.name: board
commands.task: serve, stop or inspect the board
usage: lingtai board start [--port <n>] [--dir <path>] [--no-open]
Serve the board pnpm build wrote beside this CLI, in this
process: the URL is printed, a browser opened, ctrl-c stops it.
From the source there is no built board:
pnpm --filter @lingtai/board dev
--port <n>    default 17820, or board.port in ~/.lingtai/config.yml
--dir <path>  a built board somewhere else
--no-open     no browser — what the service’s job passes
lingtai board stop
Stop the board this machine is running. Not shutdown, which
waits for an attempt. Where a supervisor keeps the board, this is
its stop, and it stays stopped until lingtai service start.
lingtai board restart
Stop, then start. Refuses nothing first: a UI at the wrong
commit costs a reload.
lingtai board status [--port <n>] [--json] [--no-color]
Who serves it, whether a board answers, whether a supervisor
keeps one — three facts, none concluded from another.

commands.name: env
commands.task: the values a project’s agents are given
usage: lingtai env set <project> KEY=VALUE
Write one value into ~/.lingtai/env/<project>.env.
lingtai env set <project> KEY
Read the value from stdin, unechoed.
lingtai env list <project> [--json] [--no-color]
Names and which layer answered — never values.
lingtai env unset <project> KEY
Remove one.

commands.name: end
commands.task: replay the end step for items that landed
usage: lingtai end replay [<project>] [--issue <n>]
Resolve the end step for items that landed, and deliver what it
resolves to. --issue limits it to one.

commands.name: approve
commands.task: merge what a held run produced
usage: lingtai approve <project> --issue <n> [--note <text>] [--json]
Merge what a held run produced, if its head has not moved since
the approval was asked for.
--note <text>   recorded with the approval, and required when a
step still refuses the head: approving then waives
each refusing step, with this as why

commands.name: answer
commands.task: answer a question a ticket was held on
usage: lingtai answer <project> --issue <n> "<choice>" [--json]
Answer it on the record: back in the queue, and every attempt at
the ticket is told the answer — no editing the issue body.
lingtai answer <project> --issue <n> [--pick <q>=<a> ...] [--json]
Answer what a step or triage asked: the answers are written into
the ticket body, then the step that asked continues on its saved
work. A question with no --pick takes its recommended answer.
examples: lingtai answer lingtai --issue <n> "use the second option"

commands.name: ask
commands.task: hold a ticket on a decision before any run
usage: lingtai ask <project> --issue <n> "<question>" [--json]
Nothing is spent, the queue passes over the ticket, and lingtai
status prints the question.

commands.name: fix-refusal
commands.task: one more implementation round on saved work
usage: lingtai fix-refusal <project> --issue <n> [--if-head <sha>] [--json]
Run one more implementation round on saved work, then repeat the
checks without waiving a refusal.

commands.name: redo-step
commands.task: run the step that stopped again, on the saved work
usage: lingtai redo-step <project> --issue <n> [--if-head <sha>] [--json]
The same attempt runs the step a crash or a red stopped again, on its
saved head: no fixer, nothing cut from base, and no round or restart
spent. --if-head refuses if the saved head is a different commit.

commands.name: start-new-attempt
commands.task: end a wait with a new run
usage: lingtai start-new-attempt <project> --issue <n> [--note <why>]
[--into-body <text>] [--json]
Queues a new attempt for a blocked item — held for approval or not —
and that attempt cuts a fresh branch from a base that has since
moved. The actor is still recorded in by.

commands.name: close
commands.task: end a ticket nobody is going to do
usage: lingtai close <project> --issue <n> "<reason>" [--json]
The queue stops offering it because the log says it is over.
Nothing lifts a close: if the work is wanted again, open a new
ticket.

commands.name: start
commands.task: hold the projections current and take work
usage: lingtai start [--no-conduct] [--no-merge] [--verbose] [--no-color]
Reads no standing signal: a pause or a shutdown aimed at an
earlier daemon was not aimed at this one. If another daemon holds
the lock this starts nothing and says so. Unchecked — lingtai
restart is the checked start.
--no-conduct   projections only, take nothing
--no-merge     as for lingtai run
--verbose      every line the conductor writes, as well

commands.name: daemon
commands.task: the old name of start, still answered
usage: lingtai daemon [--no-conduct] [--no-merge] [--no-color]
Still answers: an installed LaunchAgent or systemd unit has this
name written into it (#159). It is lingtai start.

commands.name: service
commands.task: keep the daemon and the board running
usage: lingtai service install|start|shutdown [why]|restart [why]|uninstall
lingtai service status [--json]
Two jobs, the daemon and the board: a LaunchAgent each on macOS,
a systemd user unit each on Linux. No service manager? run
lingtai daemon and lingtai board start in the foreground.
shutdown drains the conductor through the log, waits for the
attempt, unloads it, then stops the board. restart is that and
start, unchecked — lingtai restart is the checked one.
status reports each job on its own: one word for both would hide
a board that is up beside a conductor launchd keeps respawning.

commands.name: restart
commands.task: drain, wait for the attempt, and start one daemon
usage: lingtai restart [why] [flags] [--no-color]
Here, or through lingtai service when a supervisor keeps it.
Refuses a commit the tracking remote does not have, a dirty
worktree, and what lingtai doctor failed on. Ctrl+C during the
wait leaves the drain standing; the next restart picks it up.
--dirty            start from a dirty worktree, having read why not
--despite-doctor   start in spite of failed doctor checks
--force, --timeout as for lingtai shutdown
--no-conduct, --no-merge
as for lingtai start; refused under a supervisor

commands.name: shutdown
commands.task: stop the daemon after the ticket in flight
usage: lingtai shutdown [why] [--force] [--timeout <duration>] [--no-color]
The attempt finishes first, so the steps and the merge lane run
too. It does not outlive the daemon it was sent to.
--force                do not wait. The agent is left running and
the next conductor kills it
--timeout <duration>   give up waiting after this and exit anyway.
Not with --force

commands.name: pause
commands.task: stop one project, or every project, taking new tickets
usage: lingtai pause [project] [--no-color]
Locks the project, or every registered project when none is named.
A person's pause carries no reason and holds until lingtai resume.
An attempt already in flight finishes; nothing new starts. The pause
is in the log and outlasts a daemon restart: it stands until
lingtai resume lifts it. Not so for lingtai run, which takes no ticket
while a pause stands, daemon or none: one already working
finishes the ticket in hand and takes no other.

commands.name: resume
commands.task: take tickets again, for one project or every project
usage: lingtai resume [project] [--no-color]
Unlocks the project. With none named it unlocks every paused
registered project and also lifts a conductor-wide pause or a
shutdown request that stands.

commands.name: ceiling
commands.task: raise today's spending ceiling
usage: lingtai ceiling raise <usd>
Raises today's ceiling to <usd> dollars, a figure above both what has been
spent and today's ceiling, at any time of the day. Lasts until midnight; the
configuration (limits.day_usd) is not changed. Refused while no ceiling
is configured, or while today's spend cannot be read.

commands.name: account
commands.task: lift an account's limit
usage: lingtai account lift <account> [--no-color]
Says an account — a runtime, or github — is no longer at its limit. Projects
that use it take work again at the next look. Appends nothing when no limit
stands. Accounts: claude-code, codex, copilot, antigravity, github

commands.name: init
commands.task: a bare machine to the board, on the wizard
usage: lingtai init [flags]
Git and the agents looked at, a store connected to and its tables
made, ~/.lingtai/config.yml written. Run it again to continue, or
to see what is set.
--store <sqlite|postgres>
the store, instead of being asked. postgres takes
--database-url with it
--database-url <url>   instead of being asked
--port <n>             the board's port, for this run.
default: 17820, or board.port
--project <github|local>  the first project, instead of being asked
--local <dir>             a directory on this machine, as the project
--github-app <create|skip>
create or skip the App, asked only when none is configured
--github-auth <gh|app|none>
how this machine reaches GitHub, asked on every run:
the signed-in gh login, the App, or none. gh is checked, not trusted
--day-usd <dollars|none>
the most one day may spend, default 100; none removes it
--claude-token <keep|skip>
the sandboxed Claude Code token, asked only where a recipe needs it
--main <branch>           the branch a local project governs
--mode <team|solo>        does anyone else work here? team is the default
--personal <branch>       team mode: the branch Lingtai works on
--tickets <github|db>     where tickets come from
--kinds <a,b,c>          which labels are work, first taken first
--agent <claude-code|codex>  which agent writes the change
--model <name>, or --model ''
the writer's model; '' for the runtime's own default
--reviewer <agent|none>      a cold reviewer, and which, or none
--reviewer-model <name>, or --reviewer-model ''
the reviewer's model; '' for the runtime's own default
--install <cmd>              what prepares a worktree, e.g. npm ci
--build <cmd|none>           a check that must pass before review;
repeat it for more than one
--check-build yes|no         try install and build once first;
--defaults skips it unless yes
--land <branch|hold>
where an attempt lands, or hold every one for a person at proposed
--refusal-fixes <n>          fixes after a refusal an attempt may buy
--conflict-resolutions <n>   merge conflict resolutions an attempt may buy
--wall <duration>            wall time per agent run, e.g. 1h
--budget <usd>               a dollar ceiling per agent run
--defaults, --yes
use the default of every question whose answer was detected or is
easy to change later. With no terminal,
this or an answer to every question is required. The checks and
the landing are printed before a project is registered, and a
run that took the defaults for an empty build or an unattended
landing stops there unless --defaults named it

commands.name: version
commands.task: the version, and which artifact is running
usage: lingtai version [--json] [--no-color]
Platform, binary or script, and the Node running it.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.task: fetch and switch to the newest release
usage: lingtai upgrade [--despite-doctor]
Fetch the newest release from GitHub Releases, check its
checksums, unpack it beside this one in ~/.lingtai/versions,
drain what conducts, then move ~/.local/bin/lingtai. Starts
nothing. With lingtai doctor, the one request to the network
this tool makes on its own account.
--despite-doctor   upgrade in spite of failed doctor checks

commands.name: rollback
commands.task: go back to an older installed version
usage: lingtai rollback [<version>]
Run ~/.local/bin/lingtai from an older version still in
~/.lingtai/versions — the newest one below the current, unless
named.

commands.name: uninstall
commands.task: remove everything under ~/.lingtai and the shim
usage: lingtai uninstall [--yes] [--nothing-conducts]
Ask once, remove everything under ~/.lingtai and the shim, then
name what it could not: the GitHub App, and the log where the
log is a server.
--yes               do not ask
--nothing-conducts  remove a conductor's state though the lock
under ~/.lingtai/locks could not be read

commands.name: doctor
commands.task: check everything that can be checked
usage: lingtai doctor [--verbose] [--json] [--no-color] [--fix]
Lists only what needs attention; --verbose lists every check, explained.
--fix is the one way doctor writes: it rewrites a recipe refused for an old
spelling (repo.base, worktree.base, take: both) as a new recipe change, and
nothing else. It cannot be combined with --json.
Exits non-zero on any failure. Under --json a failing report is still the
report document, on exit 1: test .error first (the report could not be
produced), then .failed.

commands.name: clean
commands.task: remove orphan worktrees and run logs no longer owed
usage: lingtai clean [<project>] [--yes] [--no-color]
Lists each worktree under ~/.lingtai/worktrees that no running attempt
uses, untouched for an hour and with no uncommitted changes, and each run
log whose ticket landed, closed or was satisfied, with its size and the
reason. Takes no lock and appends nothing. Whatever cannot be read is
listed as could not be checked and kept, and the exit is 1.
--yes               remove what is listed

commands.name: projection
commands.task: how far projections lag, and rebuild one
usage: lingtai projection lag [--json] [--no-color]
How far each projection is behind the log.
lingtai projection rebuild <name>
Drop the table, reset the checkpoint, replay.
Projections: task_view, finding_backlog, spend, ticket_report

commands.name: events
commands.task: the events this version writes, by step
usage: lingtai events [<name>] [--json] [--no-color]
Reads the list bundled with this version; needs no project and no
network.
--json  the manifest instead of the sections

commands.name: token
commands.task: set the token a sandboxed Claude Code or Copilot run holds
usage: lingtai token claude
Runs `claude setup-token` for you and writes what it prints to
claude.oauth_token in ~/.lingtai/config.yml (0600), keeping every other
key. If that cannot be read from its output, asks you to paste the
token at a hidden prompt. A token already set is asked about: replace
or keep. LINGTAI_CLAUDE_OAUTH_TOKEN, when exported, wins over the file.
Needs a terminal. The token is never printed, logged or put on a
command line.
lingtai token copilot
Asks, at a hidden prompt, for a fine-grained personal access token
(github_pat_…) with the Copilot Requests permission and writes it to
copilot.github_token in ~/.lingtai/config.yml (0600), keeping every other
key. A classic ghp_ token, which Copilot ignores, is refused by name.
LINGTAI_COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN, when exported, wins over the file. Needs a
terminal. The token is never printed, logged or put on a command line.
